use_case_summary: LodenWave wants to migrate primary in-app assistant and doc-search from current LLM vendor to Redwood. Primary goals: maintain prompt-parity, reduce per-token cost on high-volume query routes, and obtain predictable latency under 200ms p95 for chat routes. Long-term plan to move high-volume traffic to Dedicated (VPC) with canary rollouts.
notes:
Account background: mid-market analytics SaaS (B2B) with ~450 employees. Product contains in-app assistant used by customers for finding docs and summarizing analytics reports. Currently on OpenAI; costs spiked as usage grew. They are cost-sensitive but care about output quality and latency.

POC specifics: we onboarded a sandbox org and ingested 2000 sample docs + 120 canonical prompts. LW engineering ran side-by-side comparisons (OpenAI vs Redwood-hosted). Observations logged: 
- Latency: Redwood p95 ~160ms for chat at sandbox load (50 RPS synthetic). Meets target.
- Cost: projected 20-35% savings on heavy embedding/search routes with Redwood's batching/caching.
- Quality: summarization prompts show regressions on 18 of 120 cases (15%). Mostly around numeric table summarization and aggressive compression.
- Function-calling & streaming: worked but needs small SDK tweaks (SE to provide quick PR).

Quoted items from LW PM: "We can't accept regressions on report summarization — customers rely on exact table numbers."

Migration ask: LW wants a compatibility strategy so product teams can flip traffic from OpenAI to Redwood with minimal prompt rewrites. They'd prefer Redwood to support an OpenAI-style compat layer or provide a migration adapter repo. Also asked about branching strategy to run A/B comparing outputs and drift monitoring.

Security: LW requires SOC2, SSO/SAML integration, audit logs exportability, and option for KMS-backed encryption for customer PII. Data residency: USA preferred.

Internal notes for RDW team: prioritize prompt-parity investigation for summarization. SE (Jon) to run targeted prompt tuning and test quantized model variants. Ask Research team for eval harness and recommended temperature/decoding settings. Offer Dedicated pool pricing with 12-month commitment and clear SLA on latency.

Next immediate actions: send POC quality report, proposed Dedicated pricing tiers, skeleton compatibility adapter repo, and schedule a deep-dive on summarization regressions with Research and LW lead (target week of 2026-03-09).
notes_on_migration:
Migration plan discussed: 1) Short-term: Redwood Hosted with an OpenAI-compat adapter layer in front of Redwood endpoints (translator service maintained by LW or provided as reference). 2) POC stage: compare outputs on 120 canonical prompts + 500 randomized customer queries; collect automatic metrics (ROUGE, token-delta, hallucination flags). 3) Tuning: model/temperature adjustments and prompt engineering to achieve parity; if regressions persist, evaluate switching to alternate model variant or using a reranker/ensemble. 4) Dedicated cutover: carve out a Dedicated GPU pool, run canary (5% traffic) for 48-72 hours, monitor latency, cost, and quality, then gradually increase. 5) Rollback & fallbacks: keep existing vendor route available as automatic fallback for failed parity checks.

Technical considerations: compat layer must map OpenAI-style completion/chat params (messages, max_tokens, temperature, function_calls) to Redwood's APIs and maintain token accounting. KV cache behavior and prefix caching need to be preserved to keep latency/cost benefits. Quantization differences were flagged as a potential cause of summarization regressions; Research team to run kernel/model selection experiments.
